resolved_conflicts.explanation: Idaho Fire Lookouts says the lookout was previously called Bird Peak; the 1929 letters call the station Bird Point Lookout and Bird Creek Lookout. Treated as one station, because the same 1929 keeper (Guntermann) is named in both.

sources.title: Early Days in the Forest Service (Volume 4): Letters to Folks Back Home, July and September 1929

notes_for_editor: Three names for one station: Bird Peak (Idaho Fire Lookouts), Bird Point and Bird Creek (the 1929 letters and the npshistory editor's note). Identification rests on the shared 1929 keeper, plus firelookout.com's placement 2.5 miles east of Shefoot Lookout, which the listed coordinates roughly fit (Shefoot Mtn is 47.30660 -115.68510). The Dave Brown 1930 entry rests on one source that cites Swiftwater People, which was not read. Built date is only 'L-4 cab' in the 1930s, so there is no built event. Dates: 1925 camp (three sources agree), 1969 destroyed (two sources agree). Brief record checked (county Shoshone, ground, destroyed 1969): no correction. Not read: Swiftwater People, other Guntermann letters in the same npshistory series, Forest Service records, any photograph. Today: no source describes the site.
